items.title: Joe Watkins Interview, 1961-01-20
items.q: And Lula White, she just had a piano player.

ctx.x: Well, would they have the bands in the houses or the cribs or the cabarets or what?

No, they were in cabarets. Yeah, you had Pete Lawless at Rice Cafe, you had Tom Anderson. And Lula White, she just had a piano player. And Tom Anderson. And Pete Barrett, they didn't have no band. And there was about four or five places around there that had bands working. Well, Henry Martin, the drummer I was telling you about, he used to work with Peter Bocas. Peter Bocas. Was it Peter Bocas? I think it was Peter Bocas. I used to work with Peter Bocas at the Rice Cafe. And that's at the corner of Iberville and…

items.title: Joe Watkins Interview, 1960-03-16
items.q: Well I had the opportunity to get in to Lula White's place

ctx.x: But that place you said, what street was it on, between St. Louis and Quarantine?

Right on the corner, at Liberty and Quarantine. Liberty, oh. Yeah, right on the corner, second catacomb from St. Louis Street Cemetery, yeah. Well I had the opportunity to get in to Lula White's place, and Emma Johnson and Willa Piazza, I used to deliver drinks to those different places, and naturally it was good money in them days, the salary wasn't much but the tips were so great, you know. Well I did fairly good, and I left from there, and right after they closed the district down in 1916 I think it was. And…
